newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to join CEFTA this year-minister.
newsitem.headline: Romania to join CEFTA this year-minister.

text.p: Romania will join the Central European Trade Agreement (CEFTA) in coming months after signing the association accord in Bucharest, Trade and Industries Minister Calin Popescu Tariceanu said on Thursday.
Negociations had been concluded on bilateral free-trade accords with the CEFTA's members, one of the key conditions for admission, Tariceanu told the independent Mediafax news agency.

Romania will become the sixth member of CEFTA, which now includes the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia and Slovenia. Bulgaria, Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia and Ukraine are also seeking CEFTA membership.
CEFTA's promotes harmonised economic development among member countries through expansion of trade. Its original goal was to set up a free trade zone by 2001.
CEFTA was set up in 1992 by Hungary, Poland and the former Czechoslovakia as a European Union-type grouping to replace the communist-era trading bloc Comecon.
